content_voiceover: For patients with high-titer inhibitors who can't use standard factor, bypassing agents restore hemostasis without needing factor eight or nine directly. The two classic options are activated prothrombin complex concentrate, APCC, and recombinant activated factor seven. APCC is dosed at fifty to seventy-five units per kilogram for joint or muscle bleeds and seventy-five to one hundred units per kilogram for life- or limb-threatening bleeds, repeated every eight to twelve or every twelve hours respectively. Recombinant factor seven a is dosed much higher on a microgram basis, ninety to one hundred twenty micrograms per kilogram repeated every two to three hours, with a high-dose single infusion option of two hundred seventy micrograms per kilogram. Remember that APCC contains vitamin K-dependent factors in both activated and nonactivated forms, which is why concurrent use with rFVIIa carries a thrombotic risk and why APCC is the agent that interacts dangerously with emicizumab.
keypoints: Bypassing agents: APCC and recombinant factor VIIa (rFVIIa)
APCC: 50-75 U/kg joint/muscle bleed, 75-100 U/kg for life/limb-threatening
rFVIIa standard dose: 90-120 mcg/kg q2-3h; high dose 270 mcg/kg once
APCC = plasma-derived vitamin K-dependent factors, activated and nonactivated
keypoint_voiceover: Bypassing agents are APCC and recombinant factor seven a.
